issue_context.title: `.str` methods silenty cast input
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
pl.select(pl.lit(1.5).str.replace("1", "2"))
# shape: (1, 1)
# ┌─────────┐
# │ literal │
# │ ---     │
# │ str     │
# ╞═════════╡
# │ 2.5     │
# └─────────┘
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Originally `.replace` was mentioned in https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/18465

It seems certain `.str` methods cast their input instead of throwing an error.

```python
pl.select(pl.date(2024, 1, 1).str.extract("(..)"))
# shape: (1, 1)
# ┌──────┐
# │ date │
# │ ---  │
# │ str  │
# ╞══════╡
# │ 19   │
# └──────┘
```

These all seem affected:

- `.str.concat`
- `.str.contains`
- `.str.ends_with`
- `.str.extract`
- `.str.find`
- `.str.join`
- `.str.replace`
- `.str.replace_all`
- `.str.starts_with`

### Expected behavior

Should raise an exception?

```python
pl.select(pl.lit(1.5).str.to_uppercase())
# SchemaError: invalid series dtype: expected `String`, got `f64`
```
